title: UNION: The Ultimate Guide
description: Learn how to use the UNION and UNION ALL operators to combine the results of two or more SELECT statements into a single result set.

data.text: SQL Server UNION: The Ultimate Guide

SQL Server UNION is one of the set operations that allow you to combine the results of two SELECT statements into a single result set that includes all the rows from both SELECT statements in the union.

data.title: UNION Syntax
data.content: Combine results of two or more queries into a single result set.

data.text: The following are requirements for the queries in the syntax above:

items: The number and order of columns must be the same in both queries.
The data types of the corresponding columns must be the same or compatible.

data.text: By default, the UNION operator removes all duplicate rows from the result sets. However, if you want to retain duplicate rows, specify the ALL keyword:

data.title: UNION ALL Syntax
data.content: UNION ALL retains duplicate rows in the result set.

data.text: In other words, the UNION operator removes duplicate rows while UNION ALL includes them in the final result set.
A JOIN such as INNER JOIN or LEFT JOIN combines columns from two tables, while the UNION combines rows from two queries.
In other words, a join appends the result sets horizontally while union appends the result set vertically.

data.title: Combine Staff and Customer Names
data.content: Use UNION to combine names from staffs and customers tables, automatically removing duplicates.
data.code:
SELECT
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM
    sales.staffs
UNION
SELECT
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM
    sales.customers;

data.text: It returned 1,454 rows. Because the result set of the union returns only 1,454 rows, it means that one duplicate row was removed by the UNION operator.

data.title: UNION ALL to Keep Duplicates
data.content: UNION ALL returns 1,455 rows including the duplicate.
data.code:
SELECT
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM
    sales.staffs
UNION ALL
SELECT
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM
    sales.customers;

data.text: To sort the result set returned by the UNION operator, place the ORDER BY clause in the last query:

data.title: UNION with ORDER BY
data.content: Sort the combined result set by first_name and last_name.
data.code:
SELECT
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM
    sales.staffs
UNION ALL
SELECT
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM
    sales.customers
ORDER BY
    first_name,
    last_name;

data.title: Tip
data.text: Use UNION ALL instead of UNION when you know there are no duplicates or when you want to keep duplicates. UNION ALL is faster because it skips the deduplication step.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: UNION combines result sets of two queries into one, removing duplicates.
UNION ALL retains duplicate rows and is more performant.
JOIN combines columns; UNION combines rows.
Columns must have matching count, order, and compatible data types.
Place ORDER BY in the last query when sorting a UNION result set.
